title: Which cell part am I describing?
objective: Describe the job of a cell part. Identify the part from a partner’s clue.

slides.title: Meet three parts of a leaf cell
body: Nucleus — contains most of the cell’s DNA.
Chloroplast — uses light to help the cell make sugar.
Cell membrane — controls what enters and leaves the cell.

slides.title: Listen to a clue
body: Mali: “This part uses light to help the cell make sugar.”
Mali: “Yes! Which words helped you guess?”
Read the dialogue once with a partner.

slides.title: Turn a clue into a sentence
body: “This part controls what enters and leaves the cell.”
Fill the gaps aloud. Use the clue to give your reason.

slides.title: Give your partner a mystery part
body: A: Choose a cell part secretly. Give one clue about its job.
B: Name the part. Say which words helped you guess.
A: Say yes or give a new clue. Then swap roles.

slides.title: One part, one job
body: Choose a part you did not describe in the last round.
Say its name and its job in a complete sentence.
Your partner listens. Did the part and its job match?
